title: Sales & CS first-look assembly and scope outline for enterprise feature bundles
creator: Carlos Mendes
description:
Purpose: Create a lightweight, repeatable 'first-look' assembly that Sales/CS can use to collect, bundle, and produce an initial scoping artifact for enterprise feature requests (non-bug). Goal is to reduce back-and-forth with PM/Eng by providing a consistent, high-signal output within one business day of intake.

Scope: Guidance, a 1-page template, a scoring rubric, and an automated routing suggestion. This covers requests that come via Sales or CS (including demo asks, customer roadmaps, and RFP-related features) and are not production incidents or bugs. We will not replace full PRDs for larger efforts; instead this supplies the input for a rapid PM triage.

Outcomes we want: faster first-response times from PM, more consistent prioritization signals (value, implementation risk, revenue runway), and higher-quality handoffs to Eng (clear acceptance criteria / success metrics).

Where artifacts live: Draft template in Confluence (https://confluence.redwood.ai/enterprise-intake/firstlook-template), sample filled worksheets in Drive (Drive -> Team/PM/IntakeExamples), and a lightweight form (Sales Hub) placeholder for collection. Links to early PRs and scripts will be added to the ticket as they land.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Sales/CS can complete the one-page intake template in <= 60 minutes for a typical enterprise ask
A2: Template includes fields: business objective, customer(s), estimate range, desired timeline, data/residency constraints, success metrics, and must-have vs nice-to-have
A3: Scoring rubric (0-10 per axis) for Value, Implementation Risk, Strategic Fit is defined with concrete examples
A4: Implementation of a triage flow doc showing routing rules (PM review, backlog, immediate engineering spike)
A5: Two pilot reps (Sales & CS) successfully use the template on live requests and provide feedback
A6: PM team defines how template output maps to next steps (quick-scope, discovery ticket, or blueprint PRD)
A7: Hand-off checklist created for Eng including known dependencies and recommended rollout modes (hosted/dedicated/private)
A8: Playbook entry created in internal handbook and linked from Sales playbook
proposal:
Proposal summary:
1) Build a single-page 'First-Look Intake' template and a short rubric doc. Use SalesHub form (MVP) to collect structured responses.
2) Scoring rubric axes: Customer Impact (revenue/retention), Product Differentiation, Implementation Risk, Compliance/Legal Complexity, Time-to-Value. Provide examples for 0/3/7/10 scores.
3) Initial routing rules: if Implementation Risk >=8 and Customer Impact <=3 => loop to PM Backlog; if Customer Impact >=8 and timeline <= 90 days => create discovery + set engineering spike request; if Compliance/Legal Complexity >=7 => escalate to Security & Legal.
4) Deliverables: Confluence template + examples, SalesHub form prototype, internal playbook page, and a short training session (30 min) for Sales/CS.
5) Pilot: run for 4 weeks with a set of 8-10 incoming enterprise asks and measure lead time to PM decision and percent of asks with sufficient detail for Eng pull-through.

Trade-offs and constraints: keep template concise to maximize adoption; deeper scoping will be a separate PRD effort. The scoring is intentionally coarse to avoid false precision. We will not attempt auto-estimation beyond t-shirt ranges in this iteration.

Measurements: adoption rate by Sales/CS, % of asks routed to correct path, average time from intake submission to PM decision, and pilot qualitative feedback.
work_items: Prototype SalesHub form and wire up to intake inbox
Create playbook entry and quick training slides
Run 4-week pilot with selected Sales & CS reps
Collect pilot feedback and iterate template
Ship final template and update PM/Eng intake workflow
comments: 2026-03-02 Carlos Mendes: Initial draft completed. Shared with Mei and Sales leadership for quick review. Confluence link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/enterprise-intake/firstlook-template (draft).

2026-03-04 Mei Chen: Reviewed draft; removed several duplicate fields and added 'Desired SLA/Timeline' as a required field. Suggested adding an explicit 'Data Residency' checkbox for regulated accounts.

2026-03-06 Alex Rivera (Sales): Suggested t-shirt estimate bracket examples aligned to ENG input (small: 1-2w, medium: 2-6w, large: 6-12w). Wants a sample email template Sales can send to customers when collecting missing info.
2026-03-09 Legal (brief): We need a flag if customer requests on-prem or dedicated deployment that might require a SOW. Marked as dependency on Security & Legal review.
2026-03-12 Mei Chen: Prototype SalesHub form live in staging; two pilot reps added. Need ENG to confirm t-shirt mapping before running pilot broadly.
2026-03-14 Carlos Mendes: Updated rubric to include example scenario for a large enterprise compliance request. Scheduling 03/17 sync with Eng leads to confirm spike process.
decisions: Keep the template to one page to maximize completion rate
Use simple t-shirt sizing for initial effort estimates rather than story points
Pilot will be 4 weeks with 8-10 inbound enterprise asks before broader rollout
open_questions: Q1: Should requests that explicitly ask for model changes (architecture-level) bypass the first-look and go straight to Research/Applied ML?
Q2: Can ENG provide a small matrix that maps t-shirt sizes to typical GPU cost/impact ranges for gross econ context?
Q3: Do we need a separate consent process if Sales collects sample customer data as part of intake?
Q4: Who owns follow-up on compliance-heavy asks if Legal review pushes to multi-week remediation?
notes: Pilot success criteria: >60% of pilot submissions have sufficient detail for PM to pick next action without >2 follow-up messages; average PM response time <48h. Next steps: finalize rubric, confirm ENG t-shirt mapping in 03/17 sync, onboard two more Sales reps to pilot by 03/19, and run pilot metrics dashboard (sheet shared in Drive).
